title: Runtime regression triage & bisect playbook
summary: Working playbook for tracking, triaging, and bisecting performance regressions in the serving runtime. Focuses on alert-first investigation, quick dashboard checks, targeted profiling, and canary-vs-baseline comparisons to isolate root causes.
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a practical runbook for on-call and on-duty eng-serving-runtime engineers to handle performance regressions (latency/cold-starts/throughput drops). It prioritizes fast, repeatable steps: confirm alert, compare canary vs baseline, collect lightweight traces, run targeted bisect, and escalate with verified artifacts.

When to use:
- PagerDuty alert for >2x p99 latency sustained for >5 minutes
- Spike in error budget consumption tied to inference route/model
- Canary failing SLA after a deploy

Quick confirmation (first 6–10 minutes):
1) Acknowledge alert in PagerDuty and post status in #runtime-incidents Slack channel (include alert link).
2) Open the runtime latency Grafana panel: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/serving/runtime-latency
   - Verify affected metric (p50/p95/p99, request rate, error rate) and time window.
   - Note whether it’s global or region-specific and which model(s)/route(s) are impacted.
3) Check rollout metadata (console -> rollouts) to correlate recent deploys/canary IDs and traffic splits.
4) Snapshot current state: take screenshots or export panels for p50/p95/p99 over last 60m and 6h.

Fast hypotheses to rule in/out:
- Recent model binary or quantization change (model version pinning wrong)
- Kernel change / container image update in serving runtime
- Host-level resource pressure (GPU throttling, CPU steal, OOMs)
- Autoscaler misconfiguration or eviction thrash
- Upstream infra (KV cache or routing) regression

Lightweight data collection (non-blocking):
- Run: kubectl get pods -n serving -l app=runtime -o wide to see restarts and node distribution.
- Query metrics:
  * PromQL for latency by route: sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{route!=""}[5m])) by (le,route)
  * Request rate by model: sum(rate(inference_requests_total[5m])) by (model)
  * GPU util by node: avg_over_time(node_gpu_utilization_percent[5m])
- Check node metrics: dmesg for OOM kills, cloud-provider console for GPU health.
- Collect a 60s perf trace on one affected pod (light sampling): curl http://pod-ip:9100/debug/pprof/trace?seconds=60 -> store as trace-<timestamp>.pprof.

Canary vs baseline quick comparison:
1) Identify the canary rollout id and baseline id from the console (or route metadata).
2) Use the per-route dashboard comparing the two traffic buckets (canary vs baseline) for p50/p95/p99 and error rate over the last 30m.
3) If canary shows regression and baseline is healthy, lock the rollout and start a bisect across commits in the canary's image/build.
4) If both canary and baseline regress, suspect infra or shared dependency; escalate to infra/SRE.

Bisect procedure (targeted commit-level):
- Preconditions: you have a reproducible regression signal in canary vs baseline and access to build artifacts.
- Strategy: binary search on commits in the suspect release window (typically last 10–40 commits).
- Steps:
  1) Identify first bad commit window: collect revision tags from the canary image (git range).
  2) Build two candidate images: midpoint commit and previous midpoint (or use existing CI images if available).
  3) Deploy midpoint as a small canary traffic split (5–10%) to a dedicated test namespace that mirrors prod load. Use the same input distribution via replay (see replay-runbook below).
  4) Compare latency profiles (p95/p99) and profiler snapshots. If midpoint is bad, repeat upper half; otherwise, repeat lower half.
  5) Stop when you narrow to a single commit.
- Notes: prefer canary bisect in a staging-like environment to avoid customer impact. If reproduction requires prod-scale load, coordinate with SRE and routing to mirror safely.

Profiler checklist (what to collect once candidate pod is identified):
- CPU: 60s perf or py-spy sampling for Python agents; collect flamegraph.svg.
- GPU: nsys/nsight capture (short 30–60s) focusing on kernels with high SM usage; capture counters: achieved_occupancy, ipc, mem_bw.
- Memory/allocators: jemalloc stats or tcmalloc profiles if applicable.
- RPC traces: collect OpenTelemetry spans for 5–10 minutes at trace-level sampling.
- KV/cache metrics: hit/miss ratio, p99 fetch time, eviction rate.
- KV trace: sample 200 requests and inspect latencies and keys.

Common fingerprints and where to look:
- Gradual p99 increase with stable p50 -> indicative of tail queuing or GC pauses. Check GC logs / thread stacks.
- Severe tail only on long-context routes -> look at KV cache behavior and kv fetch latency, sequence length handling in kernel selection.
- Uniform shift in p50/p95 -> likely systemic CPU/GPU contention or a compiler/kernel degradation. Check node-level CPU steal and kernel changelogs.
- Error rate rise with latency -> possibly resource saturation or transient dependency timeouts. Check request timeouts and downstream queues.

Alert triage checklist (to create/update alerts):
- Ensure alerts reference a route/model label and include a severity with runbook link.
- Suggested thresholds (examples, tune per route):
  * p95 > 500ms for 5 minutes AND request_rate > 50 rps -> sev2
  * p99 > 1.2s for 5 minutes -> sev1 (investigate immediately)
  * increase in error_rate by >2x over 10m -> sev2
- Add a guard to avoid noisy alerts from cold-start bursts: require sustained breach for 5 minutes or correlation with request_rate.

Replay-runbook (for reproducing):
- Use the traffic-replay tool: replay --source=prod-logs --filter=route:embedding --start=2024-10-31T12:00Z --duration=00:30:00 --target=staging-runtime
- When replaying, control QPS to match prod peak or use scaled-down faithful distribution. Capture identical headers that affect routing/model selection.

Escalation and handoff:
- If bisect narrows to a commit: open a JIRA ticket with commit hash, perf artifacts (traces, flamegraphs), and steps to reproduce. Assign to owning service/product/ML team.
- If infra-level: page SRE and attach node-level metrics and instance ids.
- For customer-impacting regressions, notify CS and include a short incident summary and mitigation plan.

Postmortem checklist (if incident):
- Timeline of events with timestamps and actions taken.
- Root cause explanation (commit/kernel/resource) and evidence (bisect result, profiler outputs).
- Mitigations: rollback, config change, patch.
- Preventative actions: alerts tuned, benchmark additions, automated bisect CI job for suspect commits.

Appendix: useful commands and queries
- kubectl logs -n serving <pod> --since=10m | grep -i "timeout"
- promql sample: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="chat"}[5m])) by (le))
- compare canary vs baseline: query grouping by rollout_id label and plot p99 as a stacked timeseries over last 60m
- profiler retrieval: scp ops@runner:/tmp/trace-<ts>.pprof ./artifacts/

Open questions / TODOs:
- Add standardized perf test harness to CI that runs a small bisect-run weekly for the main runtime repo.
- Instrument skipping logic in alerts for expected cold-start windows.
- Investigate adding automated commit-level bisect integration with CI that can trigger on canary regressions.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working playbook: please add route-specific thresholds and any missing commands you use in practice. If you have a favorite profiler snippet or promql shortcut, append it to the appendix.

Recorded references:
- See linked Grafana dashboard for canonical panels.
- Related Confluence page: CONFLUENCE-RT/Perf-Investigations
